title: Payment of Fines by Keppel Offshore and Marine to Settle Bribery Probe
what_it_is: Payment of Fines by Keppel Offshore and Marine to Settle Bribery Probe

sections.label: Keppel corruption case parliamentary questions
sections.summary: Questions asked the Minister for Law about the Keppel Offshore and Marine corruption case, including the US$422 million penalty, investigations, and government-linked companies.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Law (a) whether the penalty of US$422 million to be paid by Keppel Offshore and Marine Ltd for corrupt payments between 2001 and 2014 to officials of Petroleo Brasileiro SA and Brazil's then ruling party was part of a three-nation plea bargain agreement, involving the United States, Brazil and Singapore, and Keppel companies; and (b) what are the considerations in reaching such arrangements, which have implications on local law enforcement and prosecutorial decisions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Law in respect of Keppel Offshore and Marine's (KOM's) agreement to pay a US$422 million fine as part of a three-nation corruption probe settlement (a) whether the US Department of Justice's (DoJ's) Deferred Prosecution Agreement on the KOM corruption probe settlement, or any other agreement, includes any condition that prevents the public disclosure of the identities of the Singaporeans who are involved; and (b) when does the Government expect CPIB and AGC to formally complete investigations and to charge the individuals in question in view of the criminal findings made against KOM by the US DoJ.

sentences.speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat
sentences.text: asked Minister for Law (a) how much more time will the Corrupt Practices Investigation Bureau (CPIB) need to complete the investigations in respect of the Singaporeans involved in the Keppel Offshore and Marine (KOM) corruption case since KOM and its wholly-owned US subsidiary, KOM USA, have agreed to pay more than US$422 million in penalty to resolve corruption charges of paying about US$55 million in bribes to secure contracts; and (b) how far back in time will CPIB go to in its investigation into the Singaporeans involved since the corrupt activities were committed as early as 2001.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Law (a) how many Singapore Government-Linked Companies (GLCs) or their subsidiaries locally or overseas have been investigated or continue to be investigated by local or overseas authorities for corrupt practices over the last 30 years; and (b) what role do the Ministry and Temasek Holdings play to ensure that GLCs or their subsidiaries do not engage in corrupt practices when conducting business overseas.

sections.label: KOM penalty under DPA
sections.summary: Under the DPA, KOM has to pay a penalty of US$422 million.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: Under the DPA, KOM has to pay a penalty of US$422 million.

sections.label: Penalty distribution among countries
sections.summary: Out of the US$422 million, 50% would be paid to Brazil, 25% to the US, and 12.5% to Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: Out of the US$422 million, 50% would be paid to Brazil, 25% to the US, and 12.5% to Singapore.

sections.label: KOM payments to Singapore Government
sections.summary: KOM must pay US$52 million to the Singapore Government within 90 days, and up to another US$52 million within three years.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: Of the US$422 million, KOM must pay US$52 million to the Singapore Government within 90 days.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: Another sum of up to US$52 million must be paid to the Singapore Government within three years from the date of the conditional warning, after taking into account any further sums to be paid by KOM to Brazilian authorities.

sections.label: International investigation timetable
sections.summary: The investigation's timetable is not a domestic case, as many different investigating agencies are involved.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: As for the investigation's timetable, this is not a case where CPIB and AGC are acting alone in a domestic case.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: This is an international case where many different investigating agencies are involved.

sections.label: AGC mutual legal assistance request
sections.summary: AGC is also working on a request for Mutual Legal Assistance.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: AGC is also working on a request for Mutual Legal Assistance.

sections.label: ST Marine officers convicted
sections.summary: From 2014 to 2017, seven former ST Marine officers were investigated, charged and convicted for corrupt payments and other Penal Code offences.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: For example, from 2014 to 2017, seven former Singapore Technologies (ST) Marine officers were investigated and subsequently charged and convicted for giving corrupt payments to secure business and for other offences under the Penal Code.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: Temasek is a shareholder of Keppel Corporation, with a minority stake of about 20%.

sections.label: Jurisdictions acting under domestic laws
sections.summary: Each jurisdiction acted under its own domestic laws but in coordination with the two other jurisdictions.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: What happened was that each jurisdiction acted under its own domestic laws, but in coordination with the two other jurisdictions.

sections.label: Coordinated global resolution
sections.summary: Each country acted in accordance with its own laws while reaching a coordinated global resolution.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: What I was seeking to establish was that each country is acting in accordance with its own laws.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: But even whilst acting in accordance with its own laws, they reached a coordinated global resolution.

sections.label: Conditional warning terms not disclosed
sections.summary: It is not practice to disclose terms of conditional warnings, which are closely aligned with the US.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: Ms Sylvia Lim wanted to know whether it was coterminous and, essentially, asking what are the terms of the conditions.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: It is not our practice to disclose terms of conditional warnings, not just for Keppel, but for all cases.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: What I can say is what I have said, which is, that it is closely aligned with what has been done in the US.

sections.label: Conditional warning in lieu of prosecution
sections.summary: A conditional warning in lieu of prosecution was given because of factors outlined earlier.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: So, the next question that arises is: do you prosecute or do you give a conditional warning in lieu of prosecution?

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: And in this particular case, it was decided to give a conditional warning in lieu of prosecution because of the factors which I had outlined earlier.

sections.label: Bribes and penalty amounts
sections.summary: The DPA states US$55 million worth of bribes and a penalty of US$422 million.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: They paid something to the tune of ─ in the DPA, it says US$55 million worth of bribes.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: They have been slapped with a penalty of US$422 million.

sections.label: Ongoing investigations into individuals
sections.summary: Investigations into the individuals are still ongoing, as explained in an earlier reply.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: With respect to the individuals, as I have explained in my earlier reply, investigations are still ongoing.

sections.label: CPIB record and Teh Cheang Wan
sections.summary: Teh Cheang Wan took his own life after CPIB investigated him, showing CPIB will act when there is cause.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: There was a Cabinet Minister, Teh Cheang Wan, who took his own life after CPIB started to investigate him.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: So, there is no doubt about CPIB's record and there is no doubt that we will take action if there is cause to do so.

sections.label: KOM sanctions and debarment
sections.summary: KOM imposed about US$8.9 million in sanctions on 12 former or current employees, and tenders state debarment rules.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: This is a matter for KOM and its board.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: But, as stated in the US DPA, KOM has imposed about US$8.9 million in financial sanctions on 12 former or current employees as part of the disciplinary process.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: Government tenders explicitly state that tenderers can be debarred if, for instance, they are convicted of corruption by our Courts.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: The directors of a disbarred company will also be debarred, and any new companies or businesses they set up during the debarment period will also not be considered for award of tenders.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: Any known facts that reflect on the commercial integrity of the supplier will be taken into account in evaluating the supplier's track record.

sections.label: Temasek stake in Keppel
sections.summary: The Government is not a direct shareholder of Keppel; Temasek owns just over 20% of Keppel Corporation.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: The Government is not a direct shareholder of Keppel.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: Temasek owns just over 20% of Keppel Corporation, which is not the entity in question here, which means that there is 80% of other shareholders.

sections.label: DPA remedial measures and discipline
sections.summary: The DPA paragraph 4(d) states the company took disciplinary action against 17 former or current employees.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: What I can say and what I can point Mr Pritam Singh to, is what is already in the public domain which is in the DPA, paragraph 4(d) – which I am sure Mr Singh is familiar with – the company has engaged in extensive remedial measures, including taking disciplinary action against 17 former or current employees in relation to the misconduct described in the statement of facts.

sections.label: Payment not from Government budget
sections.summary: The payment would not come out of the Government budget.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Will it be paid from our Government budget?

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: It would not come out of the Government budget.

sections.label: KOM illegal earnings and clawback
sections.summary: Speaker asks if KOM's illegal earnings and dividends should be clawed back via forensic audit, and lists factors guiding the Public Prosecutor's decision.

sentences.speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
sentences.text: Third, would the Senior Minister of State not agree with me that the money earned by KOM through illegal and corrupt means are highly improper, and would the Senior Minister of State not agree that the dividends paid out by KOM who knew very well that its earnings were derived from bribing people and the political party in power would also be deemed illegal, and would then need to be clawed back from members of senior staff, board of directors past and present, and the only way to ascertain the amount is through a forensic audit?

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: I said how the Public Prosecutor decides will depend on several factors; so not just one factor but several.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: It includes the culpability of each individual, the available evidence, what is appropriate in the circumstances, the knowledge of each individual, the extent of his involvement, his motivations, any personal benefits he obtained, the circumstances under which relevant acts took place and any cooperation rendered.

sections.label: US$422 million disgorgement by company
sections.summary: Speaker says the company will pay out US$422 million and that monies improperly obtained have effectively been disgorged.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: As I have said, US$422 million is going to be paid out by the company.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: Insofar as the individuals are concerned, I have already pointed to the fact that in the DPA, it has been disclosed that the company has gone against the individuals.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: So, basically, as far as any monies that should not have been obtained, were obtained, they have actually, effectively, been disgorged.
